title: Launch shift binder - crew rotations & communication slate (Apr 2026) - WIP
body:
Purpose:
This binder centralizes who is working which shifts, how we communicate during the rollout, and the minimal run-of-show checklist for each shift. Designed for a 72-hour staggered launch of the model-serving change (traffic split + new batching kernel).

Context / scope:
- Release: model-serving kernel update + routing policy (traffic weighted to new pool).
- Window: 2026-04-18 10:00 UTC start (canary), 72-hour ramp to 100% if no major incidents.
- Goal: safe, observable ramp with clear handoffs, pre-defined rollback paths, and concise comms for customers and internal teams.

Who needs this binder:
- Launch conductor (owner): Jordan Patel
- Ops crew: crew rotation (below)
- Oncall SREs and Serving runtime engineers
- Product liaison for customer comms

Crew rotations (high level) - 12h shifts (local handover at shift boundary):
Shift A (UTC 08:00 - 20:00): Priya Rao (lead), Marcus Chen, shadow: Ellen R.
Shift B (UTC 20:00 - 08:00): Samir Gupta (lead), oncall SRE, shadow: Jordan P.
Notes: daytime shift to handle most rollout and metrics; night shift focuses on stability and slow ramp if needed. Each shift must produce a 6-line shift summary in the #release-ops Slack thread at handover.

Communication slate (before / during / after):
- Pre-launch (48h): email to beta customers + status page note prepared by Product (template in linked Confluence).
- T-minus 2h: Post to #release-ops: short checklist + expected milestones.
- During launch: primary channel #release-ops, backup channel #platform-incident. PagerDuty alerts to eng-sre rotation.
- Customer-facing updates: status.redwood.ai incident page + weekly rollout note if degradation noted.
- Post-mortem comms: one-line summary in #company-announcements after stabilization.

Shift run-of-show (compact checklist for each shift):
1) Pre-handoff read: previous shift summary + open action items.
2) Verify cluster health dashboards (latency P50/P95, token-per-second, GPU utilization) - baseline snapshots saved to /release-metrics/snapshots/<timestamp>.
3) Run smoke harness: 10 representative prompts across 3 models (short/long/contexted). All responses must match expected latency thresholds and no silent errors.
4) Validate KV cache eviction rates and prefix cache hit ratio (target > 65%).
5) Confirm traffic split % in the router matches schedule (canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 60% -> 100%). If any error > 5% increase in error rate vs baseline, pause ramp.
6) Check telemetry ingestion pipeline and sampling (no >30s lag).
7) If issues: escalate to release conductor + run rollback matrix.
8) Handover note posted to #release-ops and attach snapshot links.

Rollback decision matrix (short):
- Severity S2 or higher OR sustained P95 latency > baseline +50% for >10m: immediate pause and evaluate.
- If user-facing errors spike >3x baseline for >5m: rollback to previous model variant in pool (20 min targeted rollback time).
- If infrastructure (GPU OOMs, kernel panics): immediate rollback and emergency postmortem.

Smoke test harness (commands and expectations) - quick reference:
- run_smoke.sh --suite=short-context --count=10 -> expect 95th < 600ms for hosted-dedicated pool
- embed_health_check.py --model=embed-v2 -> vector dim sanity + variance within expected range
- reranker_validation.ipynb (light) -> consistent ranking for gold set (no regressions)

Telemetry & dashboards to watch (minimum):
- Serving: token/sec, avg batch size, queue depth, KV cache hit %
- Latency: P50/P90/P95, tail lat distribution, model step breakdown (embed, decode)
- Errors: 4xx/5xx by component, model backend errors, OOM counts
- Cost proxy: tokens billed per minute (sanity check against expected)

Release notes draft (customer-facing):
- Short: "We’ve deployed an inference runtime update that reduces median generation latency and enables more efficient batching for lower per-token cost."
- Details (optional): "Improved kernel selection for attention ops, experimental prefix caching enhancements; rolling ramp to 100% over 72 hours. If you see regressions, contact support@redwood.ai with subject 'Release 2026-04 - latency' and include request id(s)."
- Known limitations: some long-context requests may see transient P95 variance during early ramp.

Calendar highlights (milestones):
- 2026-04-16: Final preflight run (full smoke + chaos-lite tests)
- 2026-04-17: Stakeholder dry run (30m) + customer comms staged
- 2026-04-18 10:00 UTC: Canary start (5% traffic)
- 2026-04-18 16:00 UTC: Quick health review -> bump to 20% if green
- 2026-04-19 08:00 UTC: Extended stability window -> 60% if green
- 2026-04-20 10:00 UTC: Full ramp (100%) if green

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Final guardrail thresholds for automated rollback (who can flip auto-roll back off?). Suggest: only release conductor + SRE lead.
- Small customer cohort to notify proactively (need list from product).

Action items (owners):
- Priya: produce preflight snapshot script and schedule (due 2026-04-12).
- Marcus: finalize smoke harness permutations + attach golden responses (due 2026-04-14).
- Ellen: draft customer-facing note + update Confluence template (due 2026-04-13).
- Samir: validate PagerDuty rota mapping and escalation playbook (due 2026-04-12).

Handover template (what each shift posts):
- TL;DR one line status (green/yellow/red)
- Key metrics snapshot (P95, tokens/sec, errors/min)
- Open actions (3 max)
- Any requests for next shift

Appendix (fast links):
- Smoke harness: https://git.internal.redwood/smoke-harness (PR #1882)
- Metrics snapshots folder: s3://redwood-release-metrics/2026-04-18/
- Rollback runbook: Confluence /pages/viewpage.action?pageId=61890

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep comm messages short — engineers ignore long posts during incidents. Use bullets.
- Night shift: don't escalate to org-wide paging unless S1.
- If rollout pauses twice on same symptom, trigger postmortem planning immediately.

Draft status: this doc is a working binder. Expect edits from SRE and Product this week. Save any change as a new version and ping @release-conductor on Slack.
